3RsEDA Women's Writing Meeting using EDA's Daily Meditations: Reflections on Recovery for prompts
This crosstalk- and critique-free meeting includes approximately 20 minutes of quiet time for writing, arts, crafts, or any other contemplative, meditative, or prayerful activities, after which we read or share on how we spent our time, and / or check in. This is a very flexible EDA meeting with freedom to mention food, drink, and other twelve-step programs by name. Our zoom room opens approximately ten minutes before the meeting for fellowshipping, and as we try to accommodate space for everybody to share, the meeting may run long. The room will also remain open after the meeting for at least ten minutes.

name: EDA Week-by-Week Step Study
address: Portland, OR, USA
notes:
EDA Week-by-Week Step Study

In this meeting we begin by reading brief selections from EDA literature on a specific step, then consider questions and writing prompts based on what we heard. We write for a few minutes, and then there's time for those who want to share what they wrote. At the 45 minute mark, we pause for brief (1 minute) "Burning Desires" -- something a member feels the need to speak aloud in order to hold themselves accountable, or to experience the group's support. We wrap up celebrating "Milestones"-- sharing with one another moments that are evidence of progress (not perfection!) in recovery.

notes:
"PNWF is a fellowship rooted firmly in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous and guided by the Twelve Traditions. This is a space where newcomers and old-timers alike can come together in unity, service, and recovery.

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, just as outlined in the program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We read directly from the Big Book, share personal experience, strength, and hope, and keep our group grounded in the spiritual principles that have helped millions find freedom from alcoholism.

Though we meet online, we’re not just a digital group — we encourage members to connect locally as well."

name: EDA Big Book Study & Discussion
address: Portland, OR, USA
notes:
EDA Big Book Study & Discussion

In this meeting we read the EDA Big Book together *slowly* (just 1-2 paragraphs at a time) and share insights (or thoughts, or confusion, or feelings) that arise in us from hearing those paragraphs. At the 45 minute mark, we have time for brief (1 minute) "Burning Desires" -- something a member feels the need to speak aloud in order to hold themselves accountable, or to experience the group's support. The last 10 minutes are for celebrating "Milestones"-- sharing with one another moments that are evidence of our progress (not perfection!) in recovery.

notes:
"PNWF is a fellowship rooted firmly in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous and guided by the Twelve Traditions. This is a space where newcomers and old-timers alike can come together in unity, service, and recovery.

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, just as outlined in the program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We read directly from the Big Book, share personal experience, strength, and hope, and keep our group grounded in the spiritual principles that have helped millions find freedom from alcoholism.

Though we meet online, we’re not just a digital group — we encourage members to connect locally as well."

notes:
If joining in-person, please find us by walking through the rear parking lot and down the stairs.
We are a Step and Traditions study group, founded in 1950 and operating continuously since then. Our meetings consist of reflections on a single Step or Tradition each week, encouraging each member to speak about his personal experience, strength and hope with respect to that week's topic (or on something else that's on his mind, if that's the case). We welcome new members and would love to have you join us, in-person* or remotely.
In the interest of the health of our members and others who use this space, we'd appreciate it if you would: Wear a mask if you are not fully vaccinated, Wash or sanitize your hands upon entering,
Refrain from attending if you have been traveling within the last 10 days and are not fully vaccinated.

3RsEDA Women's Eating Disorders Anonymous Big Book Study Meeting
This crosstalk-free meeting focuses on reading and discussing the Eating Disorders Anonymous Big Book, while allowing time for general sharing and check-in. This is a very flexible EDA meeting with freedom to mention food, drink, and other twelve-step programs by name. Our zoom room opens approximately ten minutes before the meeting for fellowshipping, and as we try to accommodate space for everybody to share, the meeting may run long. The room will also remain open after the meeting for at least ten minutes.

"PNWF is a fellowship rooted firmly in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous and guided by the Twelve Traditions. This is a space where newcomers and old-timers alike can come together in unity, service, and recovery.

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, just as outlined in the program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We read directly from the Big Book, share personal experience, strength, and hope, and keep our group grounded in the spiritual principles that have helped millions find freedom from alcoholism.

name: EDA Tools, Concepts and Suggestions
address: Portland, OR, USA
notes:
EDA Tools, Concepts and Suggestions

In this meeting we begin reading brief selections from EDA literature on one EDA tool, concept, or suggestion, then consider questions/prompts based on those readings. (These are drawn from the EDA literature, and include themes such as: Basic Needs, Balance, Feelings/Not Food, "Numbers are a Distraction!", Milestones, etc.). We write for a few minutes, and then there's time for those who want to share what they wrote. At the 45 minute mark, we pause for brief (1 minute) "Burning Desires" -- something a member feels the need to speak aloud in order to hold themselves accountable, or to experience the group's support. The last 10 minutes are for celebrating "Milestones"-- sharing with one another moments that are evidence of progress (not perfection!) in recovery.

name: Pacific Northwest Fellowship
address: Issaquah, WA, USA
notes:
"PNWF is a fellowship rooted firmly in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous and guided by the Twelve Traditions. This is a space where newcomers and old-timers alike can come together in unity, service, and recovery.

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, just as outlined in the program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We read directly from the Big Book, share personal experience, strength, and hope, and keep our group grounded in the spiritual principles that have helped millions find freedom from alcoholism.

Though we meet online, we’re not just a digital group — we encourage members to connect locally as well."

name: Anchored in Healing
address: Anchorage, AK, USA
notes:
Join us for a weekly support meeting focused on recovery from eating disorders. Meetings are open to anyone struggling with an eating disorder or disordered eating, whether diagnosed or self-identified, and those in recovery.

In this group, you’ll find a safe, welcoming environment to discuss challenges, set goals, and gain support. No judgment, no pressure—just compassionate understanding from peers on a similar journey. Together, we focus on rebuilding self-acceptance, mental and physical health, and a balanced relationship with food.

Whether you’re beginning your journey or have been on the road to recovery for some time, you’re welcome to join. Together, we can work toward freedom from eating disorders and support each other in recovery.

name: Pacific Northwest Fellowship
address: Issaquah, WA, USA
notes:
Open meetings are available to anyone interested in Alcoholics Anonymous’ program of recovery from alcoholism. Nonalcoholics may attend open meetings as observers.

"PNWF is a fellowship rooted firmly in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous and guided by the Twelve Traditions. This is a space where newcomers and old-timers alike can come together in unity, service, and recovery.

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, just as outlined in the program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We read directly from the Big Book, share personal experience, strength, and hope, and keep our group grounded in the spiritual principles that have helped millions find freedom from alcoholism.

Though we meet online, we’re not just a digital group — we encourage members to connect locally as well."

When we say young people, we mean anyone with room to grow. There is a rotating format. Please bring your own big book and consider donating big books or other AA approved literature. There will be a collection box at the meeting.

name: 3Rs: Writing
address: Philadelphia, PA, USA
notes:
Zoom ID: 858-0503-9409
Passcode: EDA4Women

We gather for approximately 90 minutes
Following the standard opening readings, members suggest and decide on three or four topics, and then we write for approximately 20 minutes, focusing on any of the chosen topics as previously mentioned, or anything related to our EDA recovery. In addition to writing, attendees are free to spend the quiet portion of the meeting doing arts, crafts, or any other activity they feel is contemplative, meditative, or prayerful.

This is a very flexible EDA meeting; we encourage stream of consciousness writing, avoiding the need to censor. Therefore, it is perfectly acceptable to mention food or drink by name and / or other Twelve-Step programs in which one participates. The last portion of the meeting is open for members to read and / or share about what they wrote or how they spent their quiet time.

This is meant to be a crosstalk-free, non-judgmental, safe environment. It is not a critique group. We encourage acceptance, acknowledgment, and appreciation of any and all sharing. All present are encouraged to share.

We keep the room open for at least ten minutes before and after the meeting for fellowshipping, exchanging numbers, etc.

name: Bliss
address: 10011 Main St, Bothell, WA 98011, USA
notes:
Each meeting will have a topic from G.S.O.-approved literature, such as the Big Book, Daily Reflections, Dr. Bob and the Good Old Timers, and, of course, the 12 Steps and 12 Traditions book.

We will enjoy laughing with (not at) each other when we hear stories of what it was like, what happened, and what it’s like now. Playful banter in short quips will be acceptable.

We will ensure any Newcomers (or ‘transplants’ who moved into the area) leave with reliable resources based on our knowledge of the Pacific Northwest’s Clean & Sober communities.

This will be a safe meeting. Any ‘predatory behavior’ will not be tolerated. For your safety, we will be happy to walk you to your car if requested when you leave the 12 & 12.

During the last fifteen minutes of each meeting, we will make sure any Newcomers who haven’t had an opportunity to share will get the chance to do so.

We’ll make the coffee - please consider bringing some snacks to The 12 & 12 Fellowship Hall, 10011 Main Street, Bothell, Washington 98011

name: Inner Family Time: Connecting the Loving Parent & Inner Child Workshop
address: Mesa, AZ, USA
notes:
WSO ID WEB1399

During this 2 hour long weekly workshop we practice connecting with Higher Power, expressing the Inner Child, and embodying the Inner Loving Parent. After an orienting/grounding practice and meditation to guide you to connect to your Higher Power, Loving Parent and Inner Child, the time is yours to play, create, dance, journal, garden or whatever else your Inner Child would like to do while witnessed and affirmed by your Loving Parent. Following a visualization to integrate all of these parts within you, time is open for those who wish to share what the experience was like for them.

*This workshop meets 1pm-3pm Eastern Time. When the US is on Standard Time it meets at 11am in Arizona. When the US is on Daylight Savings Time it meets at 10am in Arizona.

** Please note that the Zoom room is always open. If nobody is there when you arrive, check to make sure you are arriving at the correct meeting time for your time zone.
